campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine: Rank by fastest progress: model capability and validation first, then changes that make every later landing cheaper, then cleanup; owner-blocked and long-horizon rows last. Consolidate duplicated logic into fewer general components rather than adding instrumentation or frameworks; net AST nodes stay flat or fall, and the clone and harness ratchets hold the floor. Delete stale data and consolidate objects to reduce surface and improve robustness and efficiency: reviewed source lives in git, derived records in OvergoDB, process state in .overgo-runtime, and nothing a tool or evidence depends on lives in tmp. A consolidation row is done only when it deletes the implementations it replaces: test the shared owner's contract, keep only meaningful caller integration checks, retire tests of deleted wrappers, and report net production and test code removed, repeated executions eliminated, gate wall time and peak memory on comparable changes. Across the 197 first-parent commits to 2026-09-23, production Go grew about 9,000 net lines and tests about 11,600. OvergoDB keeps its core -- immutable content, a durable journal, aliases, rebuildable projections -- and the repository simplifies how it uses it, in order: integrity and blocking defects, one publication path, bounded queries, one record per transition, bounded memory, declared storage policy, then bounded segments. Store rows report bytes and records added per landing, records scanned per query, open and replay time, writer wait, peak memory and compaction write volume. No new model family, workflow, optimizer or orchestration framework without an owner request. A step's verify is its machine check; a check whose prerequisite cannot run records UNAVAILABLE, not a pass. depends_on names real producers. GUI and audio keep their lanes; master runs as master-lead. docs/plan.json is the only live plan. Improvement is what the user-facing scorecard measures (owner 2026-09-27): a row states the user-visible effect it predicts, naming a scorecard metric where it can, and work that moves only internal metrics states why it exists. Consolidation onto shared paths is how one fix reaches every model.

items.title: Unexport the names no other package names, then delete what Go's dead-code analysis finds

budget.reason: a deletion: what deadcode finds in evaluation and server

steps.title: Unexport the names no other package names, then delete what Go's dead-code analysis finds
steps.rationale:
Review feedback 2026-09-28. About half the exported names in several core packages are never named outside their own package (upper bounds, since a returned type can be used without being named):

| Package | Never named outside | Exported |
|---|---|---|
| evaluation | 158 | 319 |
| server | 88 | 107 |
| projector | 86 | 120 |
| model | 80 | 160 |
| latentvideo | 71 | 122 |

Once unexported, unused code is reported by standard Go analysis. Both gopls and deadcode are installed in ~/go/bin. A deadcode run over ./... on 2026-09-28 found 836 functions no command reaches, 493 of them exported. The largest counts:

| Package | Unreachable | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| repoanalysis | 80 | the authority ratchets, run only as tests |
| runrecord | 57 | |
| diffusionimage | 52 | unwired trainer |
| controllertrain | 37 | unwired trainer |
| seq2seq | 33 | unwired trainer |
| adaptiveparity | 32 | test-only reference |
| trainingprogram | 31 | |
| devicemath | 31 | |
| testutil | 30 | test helpers |
| server | 28 | |
| workflowruntime | 23 | |
| webuilane | 22 | |
| rae | 22 | until rae-image-capability serves it |

An unwired trainer or inference path is wired, never deleted (capabilities-not-dead-code). Everything else deadcode reports is deleted.

How to land it:
- Rename with gopls, package by package, largest share first, each a net-deleting landing: evaluation and server first.
- model and projector are on the inference surface, and latentvideo is a pinned media runtime path. Each of those lands with its evidence refresh and a reviewed delta.
- The rules stage's unconsumed-exports check already keeps new exports from growing the set.

Progress 2026-09-28, the evaluation slice:
- scratchpad/unexport's finder (standard library: the package's declarations against every importing file's selectors) listed 397 names, and gopls renamed 395. Two conflicts were refused: FailedObservation and RetrievalMetrics collide with same-named functions.
- deadcode then reports 17 unreachable evaluation functions. The media, preference and text target-plan compilers and scorers are the unwired held-out objective paths the heldout-*-slice rows wire in, so they are not deleted. compositeGenerationQualityAuthority.Evaluate/Parse, PublishEvaluationEvidence, ExactPlan.Identity and productionCapabilityEntry.surface have test callers only; decide each with its owning row.
- Landed: evaluation (259 renamed) and server (84; the earlier 567 counted test-file declarations). Next: runrecord (on the inference surface), then model, projector and latentvideo with their evidence refresh.

Owner direction 2026-09-28:
- Unexporting is only the means; the value is the deletion. This row does not close on renames. Its deadcode step deleted what the analysis found in evaluation and server: 351 production and 240 test lines, including the whole unused composite-generation-quality authority.
- A behaviour-neutral rename across many files reaches every lane's closure; the evaluation and server renames cost 51 minutes of lanes. Each remaining package's rename and dead-code deletion therefore land together, paying the lane cost once per package, and no further package is unexported until the previous deletion has landed.
- The finder, rename script and legacy-form probe are in the session scratchpad (unexport/). Before a package's landing, run compatibility -refresh-identities, go test ./internal/repoanalysis and go fix on the package.

items.title: Resolve test models through store registrations instead of per-model environment variables

budget.reason: modeltest's store resolver by architecture and the test-helper consumer rule

steps.title: Resolve test models through store registrations instead of per-model environment variables
steps.rationale:
Review feedback 2026-09-28, verified. Tests read 145 distinct OVERGO_* variables. 27 of them name a model (OVERGO_QWEN3_MODEL, OVERGO_QWEN35_MODEL, OVERGO_GEMMA4_TARGET_MODEL, OVERGO_WAN_MODEL and the rest), mostly in internal/inference's runner_integration_test.go and chat_test.go. Each test is skipped unless someone sets its variable, so in practice these tests do not run.

The construction:
- internal/modeltest.Directory already resolves a model by directory name from the store's registrations.
- Add modeltest.GGUF(t, architecture): the smallest registered GGUF whose header declares that architecture. Headers are read once per process, about 30 s for the whole store.
- It was drafted and probed on the real store 2026-09-28: qwen35, qwen2, gemma4 and llama resolve; gemma3, t5, kimi-linear, cohere2, step35, wavtokenizer-dec and hunyuan-v3 have no registered GGUF and skip as not applicable.
- Caution: the smallest qwen35 is the 1-bit Bonsai-27B quant. A test that checks one model's outputs names that model through Directory rather than asking for the architecture.

Migrate each test to modeltest and delete its variable, one variable per slice. This overlaps models-out-of-adaptive-new, which drops the variables that point into adaptive_new; this row takes the rest.

The review also counted 608 command flags (cmd/recipe 78, cmd/train 76). cmd/train's flags consolidate with trainer-shared-run's shared flag set, and the rest with simplify-command-surface.

items.title: Give every train route one shared run that bounds the loop, observes the session and publishes a checkpoint

budget.reason: the shared bounded run, session and checkpoint publish, hybrid-stack's weight writer, and the loop's per-landing gate directory

steps.title: Give every train route one shared run that bounds the loop, observes the session and publishes a checkpoint
steps.rationale:
Review feedback 2026-09-28, verified; the review ranked it the largest gap for the purpose.

What publishes today:
- Only the dense workflow (trainingworkflow/workflow.go) and the audio input projection (audio.go, then PublishInputProjection) publish through trainingprogram.PublishCheckpoint.
- mixture, flow-organ, dit, mot, graft, hybrid-stack, seriesforecast, tabular and oscillatorimage train, print a loss and discard the weights.
- adapter writes plain safetensors, and only with -out.
- The held-out objective paths (RunHeldout) publish a verdict, not weights.
So the loop cannot judge or promote what those routes train.

The bounded loop has ten copies in cmd/train, about 350 lines:
- Five near-identical: mixture, flow-organ's head stimulus, latent bridge and flow head, and seriesforecast. Each steps, checks for finite values, requires a first-step gradient, calls AdmitStepWall and requires the loss below the first.
- Two variants with per-step observation: mot and dit.
- Three materially different: flow-organ's ternary with two descents, hybrid-stack's in-trainer callback, and oscillatorimage.
- workflow.go's stepGuard reimplements AdmitStepWall.
Session admit and finish has three near-identical route copies (mot, dit, hybrid-stack) and heldout_run's variant, about 150 lines.

The change:
- One shared run owns the bound, the observer session and the checkpoint publish, and every route calls it.
- The three different loops keep their bodies and use the shared run for the session and the publish only.
- hybridtrain's Checkpoint option, read but set by no production caller, gets its caller.
- The routes share one flag set; cmd/train carries 76 flags.
- Net-deleting, no framework first.
Wiring each test-only trainer is then a short route: seq2seq-trainer-to-tests, wire-bank-trainer, retire-controller-cluster, wire-media-trainers.

Predicted effect: every trained route leaves a checkpoint the loop can evaluate on held-out cells and promote, so held-out-quality becomes measurable for what they train.

steps.title: Fill the scorecard: the absorbed benchmark and validation work
steps.rationale: Absorbs, 2026-09-27: model-regression-baseline (full text catalog, both prompt shapes, required contexts, rates and peak/retained memory under budgets, accepted record ids pinned), benchmark-completion (compare only cells whose checkpoint, precision, split, shots, template, scoring and extraction agree; keep the 100-case MMLU label; TestAcceptedPublishedComparison rejects omitted cells, duplicates, stale identities and failed outcomes), final-model-validation (a bounded long-lived server run: concurrency, context grow and shrink, cancellation, failure, reload, VRAM plateauing within budget), benchmark-27b (operator only, -budget 3h per launch, resuming exact remaining cases; the row reads completed evidence and never starts the pass), gemma-12b-accuracy (the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it was downloaded 2026-09-28 on the owner's answer, to compare with the 12B FP8 twins, which score 0.5-1.2 nats per token worse than E4B on the guard corpus while overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers reference, so the suspect is the third-party quant) and validate-all-models (RAE is the remaining unvalidated model, rae-generation-path). Done when every model's row has every cell measured or carrying a stated reason. Correction 2026-09-28: the lanes are not off the landing path. d836b7deb put them back, and the landing now runs eight lanes (device, webui, model-journey, audio, thoughtbank, integration, cuda, e4b) when a change reaches them. Owner answer 2026-09-28: the full scorecard runs from the loop when the plan empties, not on a schedule. The scheduled step landed that path: validate -run, then validate -scorecard -publish writes a record beside the store with what moved since the previous one. What it still lacks, taken on here: validate -run binds a re-acquisition command only for the guard. Each modality run the scheduled step named needs its own command before the loop's scorecard measures it rather than reads old records: tabular, vqa, projection, training, activity detection, every model that is not its task's smallest, and latent-image scratch seeding.

items.title: Resolve a media request's capability once and stop routing media through the text generator

steps.title: Resolve a media request's capability once and stop routing media through the text generator
steps.rationale:
Review feedback 2026-09-28, verified in part.

Listings per request:
- In cmd/server, one native image, video or speech request lists the generation capabilities three times:
  - nativeWorkflowRequest;
  - WorkflowWorkspaceSet.ExecuteWorkflow, which re-lists every workspace until one matches;
  - StoreGenerationWorkspace.ExecuteWorkflow.
- cmd/swap's idle runtime lists them twice.
- generation_store_workspace.go then resolves the selected capability once more, unconditionally.

Cost of a listing: it is limited to the media tasks, with file presence memoized, not every model as the review said. Per generation model it still runs, under the workspace lock:
- a store refresh;
- the alias query;
- the active-record read;
- the runtime policy and active execution resolutions;
- the controls.

Routing:
- Media reaches the handler only through h.generator.(WorkflowWorkspaceAPI) on the text Generator.
- That forces the serverRuntime, remoteRuntime and idleRuntime wrappers; idleRuntime embeds GenerationRefused to pose as a generator.
- The same assertion appears in four more handlers.

The change:
1. Measure the listings' share of a real media request's first output.
2. Resolve once and pass the selection through.
3. Give the handler the workspace directly.

Predicted effect: first-output on media requests improves by the measured listing cost, and about 150 lines go.

items.title: Judge text generation objectives on held-out text targets

steps.title: Judge text generation objectives on held-out text targets
steps.rationale: The text target scorers (CompileTextTargetPlan, ScoreTextTargets: continuation likelihood, generated answer, structured validity, OCR fields, VQA rules) restored in c99544b6 judge what a text model generates, not next-token accuracy, so token-accuracy objectives do not use them. Wire them for objectives whose output is generated text: run the base and trained model's generation over held-out prompts, score with the scorer the objective declares, and judge through a text target verdict. Unlimited-OCR (OCR fields) and a generated-answer objective are the first users. items.title: Wire or delete the automation and peer workspaces no command opens

steps.title: Wire or delete the automation and peer workspaces no command opens
steps.rationale:
Found 2026-09-28 by the unexport-and-deadcode pass on internal/server.

Two whole server features have never been opened by any command:
- the automation workspace (automation_workspace.go and automation_webhook.go): webhook-triggered automations with inventory, define, activate, run, schedule and history;
- the peer workspace (peer_workspace.go): enroll, heartbeat, placement and reconcile of spillover peers.

automation_routes.go serves their HTTP routes by asserting h.generator.(automationWorkspaceAPI), which nothing implements, so each route answers that the workspace is absent. Once their config types were unexported, deadcode reports every method unreachable.

Decide by what they front. If the workflow runtime's automation and peer placement (workflowruntime, capabilityruntime's peer invocation) have users the product needs, wire each workspace into cmd/server's launch declaration (Workspaces) with a journey test. Otherwise delete the workspaces, their routes and the runtime parts only they reach. Recommendation: delete. Neither has been reachable since it was written, and no model capability depends on them. The kept trigger authority rule that names receiveAutomationWebhook goes with them.

items.title: Keep goldens in git under one provenance manifest and delete their Python generators

steps.title: Keep goldens in git under one provenance manifest and delete their Python generators
steps.rationale: Owner direction 2026-09-26. 177 tracked goldens (4.3 MB, the largest about 1 MB) stay where they are in git -- fixtures/ and package testdata -- because git is the durable, pushed copy, the store is local and has been rebuilt, a golden in git never makes its test skip, and moving them would churn the tests and the records that pin them. What they lack is provenance. One manifest in fixtures/ records, for each golden, its upstream repository and commit, its checkpoint identity, its input digest and its own digest; TestGoldensHaveProvenance refuses a golden without an entry or whose bytes differ from it. The upstream output itself is kept, not just a parity verdict: kernels legitimately move numbers, and only the upstream output re-checks parity after each move without re-running Python, where comparing against overgo's own old output would stack tolerances. The Python generators are deleted -- internal/parity/testdata/make_olmoe_tiny.py and those in tmp (timesfm3_golden.py, dinov2_golden.py, generate_kimi_k3_rank_reference.py and their inputs) -- because the manifest names what to re-run if upstream ever changes; no Python is tracked. A served model should hold the same claim, so a lane waits for it and names it (01cbf544) instead of timing out. 2026-09-25: the device lane of 69368990 failed 'physical resource is already reserved' in devicemath while two other gate processes held the GPU, and passed unchanged on re-run; a claim every GPU user takes turns that into a wait with a named holder instead of a failed lane and a manual re-run. Found 2026-09-26: every CUDA context already takes the shared device claim (driver.ContextCreate calls processcontrol.ShareResource), so a served model holds it for its context's life, and a timed-out exclusive wait already names its holders (01cbf544, TestResourceWaitNamesItsHolders). items.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path

steps.title: Move live-evidence acceptance tests off the landing path
steps.rationale: Owner review 2026-09-27. Measured: 088a4774c's test stage re-ran 17 suites for 6 min 56 s (audioparity 376 s, cmd/compatibility 192 s, capabilityruntime 122 s, modelintake 119 s, server 71 s) because plan -stop had written a record into the live store at 17:56:23; the next plan-only landing, with no store write before it, ran 4 packages in 40 s. Suites that read the live store re-run on every store write, and their verdict depends on the machine's store rather than the commit. The gate runs go test with OVERGO_DATA_ROOT pointing at an empty scratch directory and OVERGO_AUDIO_REFERENCE_STORE unset (construction: no test can reach the live store through the environment); the 16 test files that name the store by path (overgodb-store, gitauthority.CanonicalOvergoDBDirectory) become hermetic on fixtures or scratch stores, or move off the landing path to the scheduled scorecard and validate, where live-store checks belong. Predicted effect: landings stop paying for store writes; a narrow landing's test stage stays near a minute. Measured 2026-09-27 before starting: with the data root pointed at an empty directory, 133 tests in 77 files across 12 packages fail (cmd/compatibility 32 files, internal/audioparity 19, internal/evaluation 10, speechsynth, server and others): retained-evidence acceptance tests and a few live model-file tests. They re-run when the evidence changes, which is correct; the measured 7-minute landing came from a control record (plan -stop) written into the evidence store, which stop-state-out-of-store removes. Moving them means splitting mixed files across 12 packages and a scheduled evidence run. Do it only if dev-loop measurement shows real evidence writes costing landings. Re-raised 2026-09-27 under landing-wall-budget: the four slowest suites a landing re-runs are these, and they re-run on dependency changes as well as store writes, so the stop-file fix alone does not bring landings under the budget. Updated 2026-09-27 after 32ad2b892: the store-write cause is gone. The data lives outside the module folder, so a store write re-runs nothing. The audio acceptances run in their own lane (780d83550). What remains is hermeticity: these suites' verdicts depend on the machine's data. That does not speed up landings, because a lane would run exactly when their code changes, as go test does now. So the row ranks after the user-visible fixes. Measured 2026-09-28 after the lanes landed: go test ./... with OVERGO_DATA_ROOT on an empty folder fails 92 tests in 12 packages: cmd/compatibility 56 (40 top-level accepted-evidence and acceptance projections, opening the store through retainedReferenceStore in 34 places and dataroot.Resolve in about 36), internal/evaluation 16, internal/speechsynth 7, internal/server 4, internal/audioparity 2, and one each in oscillatorimage, modelintake, dataset, capabilityruntime, cmd/smoke-lane, cmd/longform and cmd/benchmark-report. The work: consolidate each package's live-store entry into one helper behind testskip.StoreAcceptance, and run the packages in a store lane (without the five failing audits, tracked in refresh-accepted-evidence). The benefit is hermeticity only: with the data outside the module, a lane runs these exactly when go test does now. Ranked after plan-tool-plain-data.

steps.rationale: Re-measured 2026-09-24 after store-open-decode-cost (180a7a3c): an open takes about 1.05-1.5 s and allocates 1.8 GB; checkpoint decode is 56% of it (lineage 0.6 s) and replaying the 8,100 commits since the last checkpoint is 32%. Before that, 2026-09-22: a read-only open is 1.7 s, bounded by the largest decode (lineage 88.3 MB of 189 MB), with verification about 0.1 s. Laziness inside the facet fails (value receivers) and re-replaying the journal fails (shared file cursor). Defer at the store, which owns the lock: keep the verified payload and pending commits, apply on first load behind a double-checked write lock, and test that a deferred facet answers exactly as an eager one.
